newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf gas oil hits new high amid term talks.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf gas oil hits new high amid term talks.

text.p: Middle East Gulf gas oil (heating oil) outright prices on Monday hit their highest level since November 1991 as leading refiners took up contract negotiations with firms for term supplies next year, Gulf traders said on Monday.
Gas oil was assessed at $27.15 a barrel fob Gulf on Monday, tracking firmer Asia and European heating fuel markets which are rallying ahead of the northern hemisphere's winter.
Singapore gas oil swap markets rallied to record highs on Monday on strong prices in the west.
"Supplies for 0.5 percent (sulphur content gas oil) are tight and buying is strong," one trader based in the United Arab Emirates.
Sellers were asking premiums of more than a dollar barrel.
Companies who want to lift gas oil and jet-kerosene from state-owed Saudi Aramco on Monday submitted their initial volume and price ideas for term middle distillate supplies.
The Indian Oil Corporation is set to begin middle distillate talks this week with Bahrain and Saudi Arabia after securing supplies from Kuwait and Abu Dhabi, traders said.
IOC agreed gas oil terms with Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) at around a 70 cents premium.
Exports of gas oil from Gulf refiners and Yemen run close to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd).
